summary: Hybrid architecture: Django + TimescaleDB serving Vue + Vite (SPA), hosted on AWS ECS on Fargate (us-east-1 N. Virginia). Estimated $2,500-9,400/month (above the $1,500 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: A modular API service for accounts, billing and persistence plus an ingestion pipeline that scale independently for 20,000 concurrent connections. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 4 engineer(s) cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web - Vue + Vite (SPA): Chosen because team already works in typescript (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5 (budget re-plan); strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=3.

alternatives.why_not: Vue + Vite scores higher on learning curve (fit 6.3 vs 6.6).
Vue + Vite scores higher on cost (fit 6.1 vs 6.6).

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in python (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3.

alternatives.why_not: Django scores higher on security and time-to-market (fit 7.7 vs 7.9).
Minimal framework leaves domain structure to the team. Django scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 6.4 vs 7.9).
Excluded by hard constraint: cloud_preference=aws: Firebase (Firestore + Auth + Functions) is a Google Cloud service.

database.justification: Chosen because time-series hypertables for device telemetry; relational integrity and transactions for a iot domain; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=5 (budget re-plan). Managed as Timescale Cloud (TigerData): managed failover/standby available.

alternatives.why_not: TimescaleDB scores higher on fit for the project type and performance (fit 6.6 vs 7.9).
TimescaleDB scores higher on fit for the project type and performance (fit 5.5 vs 7.9).
Excluded by hard constraint: cloud_preference=aws: Google BigQuery is a Google Cloud service.
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud: self-managed VMs/databases are excluded in favour of managed services.

tradeoffs: Managed service availability varies by region
Timescale Cloud (TigerData) starts around $600/month against a $1,500/month total budget

hosting.choice: AWS ECS on Fargate (us-east-1 N. Virginia)
hosting.justification: Chosen because strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; runs the Django (Python) container as-is; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=3.

alternatives.why_not: Weaker maintainability (2/5) with priorities.maintainability=3. AWS ECS on Fargate scores higher on scalability and security (fit 2.8 vs 3.6).
Over-engineering for 1,000 users (pays off beyond ~1,000,000); Managed Kubernetes (EKS / GKE / AKS) starts around $1,200/month against a $1,500/month total budget (fit -3.8 vs 3.6).
Excluded by hard constraint: cloud_preference=aws: Google Cloud Run is a Google Cloud service.

tradeoffs: VPC, load balancer and NAT setup add fixed cost and complexity

supporting.justification: Chosen because same cloud/platform and region as the application; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=3; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosting another service when a managed option exists. Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey scores higher on integration with the hosting platform and scalability (fit 2.8 vs 6.2).
Excluded by hard constraint: cloud_preference=aws: Azure Managed Redis is a Azure service.

warnings.message: Estimated minimum $2,500/month exceeds budget.monthly_infra_usd=$1,500. Biggest drivers: Timescale Cloud (TigerData) (~$1,285), AWS ECS on Fargate (us-east-1 N. Virginia) (~$500). The stack shown is already the cost-optimised plan.

To respect priorities.cost=5 the database runs as a single-zone primary with automated backups; single-zone managed SLAs are ~99.5%, below the 99.9% target. Enabling the HA standby roughly doubles the database line item.

assumptions: No data_residency or user geography given; primary region defaults to US East (move it next to your users)

Budget re-plan: the first plan's floor (~$2,850/month) exceeded budget.monthly_infra_usd=$1,500, so the engine re-ran with cost weighted at 5 (input priorities.cost=3) and kept the cheaper plan (~$2,500/month)
RELAXED budget.monthly_infra_usd: requirements as stated need at least ~$2,500/month; raise the budget or reduce scope (fewer platforms, lower availability, defer search/realtime features)
